verses.decoded: The officials came to apologize, escorted them out, and asked them to leave the city.

verses.kjv: And they went out of the prison, and entered into the house of Lydia: and when they had seen the brethren, they comforted them, and departed.
verses.decoded: Paul and Silas left the prison and went to Lydia's house. After encouraging the believers there, they left.

verses.kjv: Now when they had passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where was a synagogue of the Jews:
verses.decoded: After traveling through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they arrived at Thessalonica, where there was a Jewish synagogue.

verses.kjv: And Paul, as his manner was, went in unto them, and three sabbath days reasoned with them out of the scriptures,
verses.decoded: As he usually did, Paul went to the synagogue and for three Sabbath days explained and discussed the Scriptures with them.

verses.kjv: Opening and alleging, that Christ must needs have suffered, and risen again from the dead; and that this Jesus, whom I preach unto you, is Christ.
verses.decoded: He explained and proved that the Messiah had to suffer and rise from the dead, and that Jesus, whom I am preaching to you, is the Messiah.

verses.kjv: And some of them believed, and consorted with Paul and Silas; and of the devout Greeks a great multitude, and of the chief women not a few.
verses.decoded: Some of the people believed and joined Paul and Silas, including many devout Greeks and several prominent women.

verses.kjv: But the Jews which believed not, moved with envy, took unto them certain lewd fellows of the baser sort, and gathered a company, and set all the city on an uproar, and assaulted the house of Jason, and sought to bring them out to the people.
verses.decoded: But the unbelieving Jews, jealous and angry, gathered some troublemakers and started a riot in the city. They attacked Jason’s house, trying to drag Paul and Silas out to the crowd.

verses.kjv: And when they found them not, they drew Jason and certain brethren unto the rulers of the city, crying, These that have turned the world upside down are come hither also;
verses.decoded: When they couldn’t find Paul and Silas, they arrested Jason and some other believers and brought them before the city officials, shouting, 'These men who are upsetting the world have come here too!'

verses.kjv: Whom Jason hath received: and these all do contrary to the decrees of Caesar, saying that there is another king, one Jesus.
verses.decoded: They said, 'Jason is harboring them, and all of them are acting against Caesar’s laws by claiming there is another king—Jesus.'

verses.kjv: And they troubled the people and the rulers of the city, when they heard these things.
verses.decoded: When the city officials heard this, they became disturbed and upset.

verses.kjv: And when they had taken security of Jason, and of the other, they let them go.
verses.decoded: After Jason and the others promised to keep the peace, the officials released them.

verses.kjv: And the brethren immediately sent away Paul and Silas by night unto Berea: who coming thither went into the synagogue of the Jews.
verses.decoded: The believers quickly sent Paul and Silas away at night to Berea. When they arrived, they went to the Jewish synagogue there.

verses.kjv: These were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so.
verses.decoded: The people in Berea were more open-minded than those in Thessalonica. They eagerly accepted the message and examined the Scriptures every day to see if what Paul said was true.

verses.kjv: Therefore many of them believed; also of honourable women which were Greeks, and of men, not a few.
verses.decoded: As a result, many of them believed, including respected Greek women and a significant number of men.

verses.kjv: But when the Jews of Thessalonica had knowledge that the word of God was preached of Paul at Berea, they came thither also, and stirred up the people.
verses.decoded: But when the Jews from Thessalonica learned that Paul was preaching in Berea, they came there too and stirred up trouble among the people.

verses.kjv: And then immediately the brethren sent away Paul to go as it were to the sea: but Silas and Timotheus abode there still.
verses.decoded: So the believers quickly sent Paul away to the coast, while Silas and Timothy stayed behind in Berea.

verses.kjv: And they that conducted Paul brought him unto Athens: and receiving a commandment unto Silas and Timotheus for to come to him with all speed, they departed.
verses.decoded: Those who escorted Paul took him to Athens. They sent a message to Silas and Timothy, asking them to join Paul as soon as possible, and then they left.

verses.kjv: Now while Paul waited for them at Athens, his spirit was stirred in him, when he saw the city wholly given to idolatry.
verses.decoded: While Paul was waiting for them in Athens, he was deeply troubled when he saw that the city was full of idols.

verses.kjv: Therefore disputed he in the synagogue with the Jews, and with the devout persons, and in the market daily with them that met with him.
verses.decoded: So he debated with the Jews and God-fearing people in the synagogue, and every day he talked with others in the marketplace who happened to be there.

verses.kjv: Then certain philosophers of the Epicureans, and of the Stoicks, encountered him. And some said, What will this babbler say? other some, He seemeth to be a setter forth of strange gods: because he preached unto them Jesus, and the resurrection.
verses.decoded: Some Epicurean and Stoic philosophers began to argue with him. Some asked, 'What is this nonsense he’s talking about?' Others said, 'He seems to be promoting new gods,' because he was preaching about Jesus and the resurrection.

verses.kjv: And they took him, and brought him unto Areopagus, saying, May we know what this new doctrine, whereof thou speakest, is?
verses.decoded: They took him to the Areopagus and asked, 'We want to know more about this new teaching you are talking about.'

verses.kjv: For thou bringest certain strange things to our ears: we would know therefore what these things mean.
verses.decoded: You are telling us things we haven’t heard before, so we want to understand what they mean.

verses.kjv: (For all the Athenians and strangers which were there spent their time in nothing else, but either to tell, or to hear some new thing.)
verses.decoded: Everyone in Athens, including visitors, spent their time talking about or listening to the latest ideas.

verses.kjv: Then Paul stood in the midst of Mars’ hill, and said, Ye men of Athens, I perceive that in all things ye are too superstitious.
verses.decoded: Paul stood in the middle of Mars' Hill and said, 'Men of Athens, I see that you are very religious about many things.'

verses.kjv: For as I passed by, and beheld your devotions, I found an altar with this inscription, TO THE UNKNOWN GOD. Whom therefore ye ignorantly worship, him declare I unto you.
verses.decoded: As I walked around and looked at your religious shrines, I found an altar with the inscription 'To the Unknown God.' You worship this God without really knowing him, and I am here to tell you about him.

verses.kjv: God that made the world and all things therein, seeing that he is Lord of heaven and earth, dwelleth not in temples made with hands;
verses.decoded: The God who created the world and everything in it, who rules over heaven and earth, does not live in temples made by human hands.

verses.kjv: Neither is worshipped with men’s hands, as though he needed any thing, seeing he giveth to all life, and breath, and all things;
verses.decoded: He is not served by human hands as if he needed anything, because he gives everyone life, breath, and everything else.

verses.kjv: And hath made of one blood all nations of men for to dwell on all the face of the earth, and hath determined the times before appointed, and the bounds of their habitation;
verses.decoded: He made all the nations from one man’s blood to live all over the earth, and he set the times and places where they would live.

verses.kjv: That they should seek the Lord, if haply they might feel after him, and find him, though he be not far from every one of us:
verses.decoded: God wants people to seek him, hoping they will reach out and find him, because he is not far from any of us.

verses.kjv: For in him we live, and move, and have our being; as certain also of your own poets have said, For we are also his offspring.
verses.decoded: We live, move, and exist because of him. As some of your own poets have said, 'We are his children.'

verses.kjv: Forasmuch then as we are the offspring of God, we ought not to think that the Godhead is like unto gold, or silver, or stone, graven by art and man’s device.
verses.decoded: Since we are God’s children, we should not think that God is like gold, silver, or stone sculptures made by human hands.

verses.kjv: And the times of this ignorance God winked at; but now commandeth all men every where to repent:
verses.decoded: God overlooked the ignorance of people in the past, but now he commands everyone everywhere to turn away from sin and change their lives.

verses.kjv: Because he hath appointed a day, in the which he will judge the world in righteousness by that man whom he hath ordained; whereof he hath given assurance unto all men, in that he hath raised him from the dead.
verses.decoded: God has set a specific day when He will judge the whole world fairly through the man He has chosen, and He has guaranteed this to everyone by raising him from the dead.

verses.kjv: And when they heard of the resurrection of the dead, some mocked: and others said, We will hear thee again of this matter.
verses.decoded: When they heard about the resurrection of the dead, some people laughed at Paul, while others said they wanted to hear more about it later.

verses.kjv: So Paul departed from among them.
verses.decoded: After that, Paul left their company.

verses.kjv: Howbeit certain men clave unto him, and believed: among the which was Dionysius the Areopagite, and a woman named Damaris, and others with them.
verses.decoded: However, some people joined Paul and believed his message, including Dionysius, a member of the Areopagus council, a woman named Damaris, and others.

verses.kjv: After these things Paul departed from Athens, and came to Corinth;
verses.decoded: After that, Paul left Athens and went to Corinth.

verses.kjv: And found a certain Jew named Aquila, born in Pontus, lately come from Italy, with his wife Priscilla; (because that Claudius had commanded all Jews to depart from Rome:) and came unto them.
verses.decoded: He met a Jew named Aquila, who was from Pontus and had recently come from Italy, along with his wife Priscilla. This was because the emperor Claudius had ordered all Jews to leave Rome. Paul went to stay with them.

verses.kjv: And because he was of the same craft, he abode with them, and wrought: for by their occupation they were tentmakers.
verses.decoded: Since Paul had the same trade, he stayed with them and worked, because they were all tentmakers by profession.

verses.kjv: And he reasoned in the synagogue every sabbath, and persuaded the Jews and the Greeks.
verses.decoded: Every Sabbath, Paul debated in the synagogue and convinced both Jews and Greeks.

verses.kjv: And when Silas and Timotheus were come from Macedonia, Paul was pressed in the spirit, and testified to the Jews that Jesus was Christ.
verses.decoded: When Silas and Timothy arrived from Macedonia, Paul was deeply compelled and boldly told the Jews that Jesus is the Messiah.

verses.kjv: And when they opposed themselves, and blasphemed, he shook his raiment, and said unto them, Your blood be upon your own heads; I am clean: from henceforth I will go unto the Gentiles.
verses.decoded: When they opposed and insulted him, Paul shook the dust off his clothes and said, 'The responsibility is yours; I am innocent. From now on, I will go to the Gentiles.'

verses.kjv: And he departed thence, and entered into a certain man’s house, named Justus, one that worshipped God, whose house joined hard to the synagogue.
verses.decoded: Paul left and went to the home of a man named Justus, who worshiped God. His house was right next to the synagogue.

verses.kjv: And Crispus, the chief ruler of the synagogue, believed on the Lord with all his house; and many of the Corinthians hearing believed, and were baptized.
verses.decoded: Crispus, the leader of the synagogue, believed in the Lord along with his entire household. Many Corinthians who heard Paul also believed and were baptized.

verses.kjv: Then spake the Lord to Paul in the night by a vision, Be not afraid, but speak, and hold not thy peace:
verses.decoded: That night, the Lord spoke to Paul in a vision: 'Don't be afraid. Keep speaking and don't be silent.'

verses.kjv: For I am with thee, and no man shall set on thee to hurt thee: for I have much people in this city.
verses.decoded: I am with you, and no one will harm you, because I have many people in this city.

verses.kjv: And he continued there a year and six months, teaching the word of God among them.
verses.decoded: Paul stayed there for a year and a half, teaching God's message to the people.

verses.kjv: And when Gallio was the deputy of Achaia, the Jews made insurrection with one accord against Paul, and brought him to the judgment seat,
verses.decoded: When Gallio was the governor of Achaia, the Jews united in protest against Paul and brought him before the court.

verses.kjv: Saying, This fellow persuadeth men to worship God contrary to the law.
verses.decoded: They accused Paul, saying, 'This man is persuading people to worship God in a way that breaks the law.'

verses.kjv: And when Paul was now about to open his mouth, Gallio said unto the Jews, If it were a matter of wrong or wicked lewdness, O ye Jews, reason would that I should bear with you:
verses.decoded: As Paul was about to speak, Gallio told the Jews, 'If this were a crime or serious wrongdoing, I would listen to you.'

verses.kjv: But if it be a question of words and names, and of your law, look ye to it; for I will be no judge of such matters.
verses.decoded: But if it’s just about words, names, or your own law, handle it yourselves. I won’t judge these kinds of issues.

verses.kjv: And he drave them from the judgment seat.
verses.decoded: He forced them to leave the judge's seat.

verses.kjv: Then all the Greeks took Sosthenes, the chief ruler of the synagogue, and beat him before the judgment seat. And Gallio cared for none of those things.
verses.decoded: Then the Greeks grabbed Sosthenes, the leader of the synagogue, and beat him in front of the judge’s seat. But Gallio didn’t pay any attention to it.

verses.kjv: And Paul after this tarried there yet a good while, and then took his leave of the brethren, and sailed thence into Syria, and with him Priscilla and Aquila; having shorn his head in Cenchrea: for he had a vow.
verses.decoded: After this, Paul stayed there for a while longer. Then he said goodbye to the believers and sailed to Syria with Priscilla and Aquila. He had his head shaved at Cenchrea because he had taken a vow.

verses.kjv: And he came to Ephesus, and left them there: but he himself entered into the synagogue, and reasoned with the Jews.
verses.decoded: He arrived in Ephesus, left Priscilla and Aquila there, and went into the synagogue to debate with the Jews.

verses.kjv: When they desired him to tarry longer time with them, he consented not;
verses.decoded: When they asked him to stay longer, he refused.

verses.kjv: But bade them farewell, saying, I must by all means keep this feast that cometh in Jerusalem: but I will return again unto you, if God will. And he sailed from Ephesus.
verses.decoded: He said goodbye, explaining that he had to go to Jerusalem to celebrate the upcoming festival, but promised to return if God allowed. Then he sailed away from Ephesus.

verses.kjv: And when he had landed at Caesarea, and gone up, and saluted the church, he went down to Antioch.
verses.decoded: After landing at Caesarea, he went up to Jerusalem and greeted the church there, then traveled down to Antioch.

verses.kjv: And after he had spent some time there, he departed, and went over all the country of Galatia and Phrygia in order, strengthening all the disciples.
verses.decoded: After spending some time there, he left and traveled through the regions of Galatia and Phrygia, strengthening all the believers.

verses.kjv: And a certain Jew named Apollos, born at Alexandria, an eloquent man, and mighty in the scriptures, came to Ephesus.
verses.decoded: A Jewish man named Apollos, from Alexandria, who was eloquent and very knowledgeable about the Scriptures, came to Ephesus.

verses.kjv: This man was instructed in the way of the Lord; and being fervent in the spirit, he spake and taught diligently the things of the Lord, knowing only the baptism of John.
verses.decoded: He had been taught about the Lord and was passionate in spirit. He spoke and taught carefully about Jesus, but he only knew about John’s baptism.

verses.kjv: And he began to speak boldly in the synagogue: whom when Aquila and Priscilla had heard, they took him unto them, and expounded unto him the way of God more perfectly.
verses.decoded: He started speaking boldly in the synagogue. When Aquila and Priscilla heard him, they took him aside and explained God’s way to him more accurately.

verses.kjv: And when he was disposed to pass into Achaia, the brethren wrote, exhorting the disciples to receive him: who, when he was come, helped them much which had believed through grace:
verses.decoded: When Apollos decided to go to Achaia, the believers wrote letters encouraging the disciples there to welcome him. When he arrived, he greatly helped those who had believed by God’s grace.

verses.kjv: For he mightily convinced the Jews, and that publickly, shewing by the scriptures that Jesus was Christ.
verses.decoded: He strongly argued with the Jews in public, using the Scriptures to prove that Jesus is the Messiah.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, that, while Apollos was at Corinth, Paul having passed through the upper coasts came to Ephesus: and finding certain disciples,
verses.decoded: While Apollos was in Corinth, Paul traveled through the inland regions and arrived at Ephesus. There, he found some followers.

verses.kjv: He said unto them, Have ye received the Holy Ghost since ye believed? And they said unto him, We have not so much as heard whether there be any Holy Ghost.
verses.decoded: Paul asked them, 'Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you believed?' They answered, 'We haven't even heard that there is a Holy Spirit.'

verses.kjv: And he said unto them, Unto what then were ye baptized? And they said, Unto John’s baptism.
verses.decoded: Paul asked, 'Then what baptism did you receive?' They replied, 'John's baptism.'

verses.kjv: Then said Paul, John verily baptized with the baptism of repentance, saying unto the people, that they should believe on him which should come after him, that is, on Christ Jesus.
verses.decoded: Paul explained, 'John baptized people as a sign of repentance, telling them to believe in the one who would come after him—Jesus Christ.'

verses.kjv: When they heard this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
verses.decoded: After hearing this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.

verses.kjv: And when Paul had laid his hands upon them, the Holy Ghost came on them; and they spake with tongues, and prophesied.
verses.decoded: When Paul placed his hands on them, the Holy Spirit came upon them, and they spoke in tongues and prophesied.

verses.kjv: And all the men were about twelve.
verses.decoded: There were about twelve men in all.

verses.kjv: And he went into the synagogue, and spake boldly for the space of three months, disputing and persuading the things concerning the kingdom of God.
verses.decoded: Paul went into the synagogue and boldly taught about God's kingdom for three months, debating and persuading people.

verses.kjv: But when divers were hardened, and believed not, but spake evil of that way before the multitude, he departed from them, and separated the disciples, disputing daily in the school of one Tyrannus.
verses.decoded: When some became stubborn and refused to believe, speaking badly about the message publicly, Paul left them and took the believers with him, teaching every day in the lecture hall of a man named Tyrannus.

verses.kjv: And this continued by the space of two years; so that all they which dwelt in Asia heard the word of the Lord Jesus, both Jews and Greeks.
verses.decoded: This went on for two years, so that everyone living in the province of Asia—both Jews and Greeks—heard the message about the Lord Jesus.

verses.kjv: And God wrought special miracles by the hands of Paul:
verses.decoded: God performed extraordinary miracles through Paul’s hands.

verses.kjv: So that from his body were brought unto the sick handkerchiefs or aprons, and the diseases departed from them, and the evil spirits went out of them.
verses.decoded: People brought handkerchiefs and aprons that had touched Paul to the sick, and their illnesses were healed and evil spirits left them.

verses.kjv: Then certain of the vagabond Jews, exorcists, took upon them to call over them which had evil spirits the name of the LORD Jesus, saying, We adjure you by Jesus whom Paul preacheth.
verses.decoded: Some wandering Jewish exorcists tried to cast out evil spirits by calling on the name of the Lord Jesus, saying, 'I command you by Jesus, whom Paul preaches.'

verses.kjv: And there were seven sons of one Sceva, a Jew, and chief of the priests, which did so.
verses.decoded: Seven sons of a Jewish chief priest named Sceva did this.

verses.kjv: And the evil spirit answered and said, Jesus I know, and Paul I know; but who are ye?
verses.decoded: The evil spirit replied, 'I know Jesus and I know Paul, but who are you?'

verses.kjv: And the man in whom the evil spirit was leaped on them, and overcame them, and prevailed against them, so that they fled out of that house naked and wounded.
verses.decoded: The man who had the evil spirit jumped on them, defeated them, and overpowered them, so they ran out of the house naked and injured.

verses.kjv: And this was known to all the Jews and Greeks also dwelling at Ephesus; and fear fell on them all, and the name of the Lord Jesus was magnified.
verses.decoded: Everyone, both Jews and Greeks living in Ephesus, heard about this, and they all became afraid. The name of the Lord Jesus was greatly honored.

verses.kjv: And many that believed came, and confessed, and shewed their deeds.
verses.decoded: Many who believed came forward, admitted their sins, and openly showed what they had done.

verses.kjv: Many of them also which used curious arts brought their books together, and burned them before all men: and they counted the price of them, and found it fifty thousand pieces of silver.
verses.decoded: Many who practiced magic brought their scrolls together and burned them publicly. When they added up the value, it was fifty thousand silver coins.

verses.kjv: So mightily grew the word of God and prevailed.
verses.decoded: The message of God grew stronger and became more powerful.

verses.kjv: After these things were ended, Paul purposed in the spirit, when he had passed through Macedonia and Achaia, to go to Jerusalem, saying, After I have been there, I must also see Rome.
verses.decoded: After these events, Paul decided, guided by the Spirit, that after traveling through Macedonia and Achaia, he would go to Jerusalem, and then he planned to visit Rome.

verses.kjv: So he sent into Macedonia two of them that ministered unto him, Timotheus and Erastus; but he himself stayed in Asia for a season.
verses.decoded: He sent Timothy and Erastus, who helped him, into Macedonia, but Paul stayed in the province of Asia for a while.

verses.kjv: And the same time there arose no small stir about that way.
verses.decoded: At that time, there was a significant disturbance about the Christian teaching.

verses.kjv: For a certain man named Demetrius, a silversmith, which made silver shrines for Diana, brought no small gain unto the craftsmen;
verses.decoded: A man named Demetrius, a silversmith who made silver idols of the goddess Diana, was bringing a lot of profit to the craftsmen.

verses.kjv: Whom he called together with the workmen of like occupation, and said, Sirs, ye know that by this craft we have our wealth.
verses.decoded: He gathered the other craftsmen and said, 'Gentlemen, you know that we make our living from this trade.'

verses.kjv: Moreover ye see and hear, that not alone at Ephesus, but almost throughout all Asia, this Paul hath persuaded and turned away much people, saying that they be no gods, which are made with hands:
verses.decoded: You see and hear that Paul has convinced many people not only in Ephesus but throughout Asia that idols made by human hands are not gods.

verses.kjv: So that not only this our craft is in danger to be set at nought; but also that the temple of the great goddess Diana should be despised, and her magnificence should be destroyed, whom all Asia and the world worshippeth.
verses.decoded: So not only is our business at risk, but the temple of the great goddess Diana might be disrespected and her glory destroyed, and she is worshiped throughout Asia and the world.

verses.kjv: And when they heard these sayings, they were full of wrath, and cried out, saying, Great is Diana of the Ephesians.
verses.decoded: When they heard this, they became very angry and shouted, 'Great is Diana of the Ephesians!'

verses.kjv: And the whole city was filled with confusion: and having caught Gaius and Aristarchus, men of Macedonia, Paul’s companions in travel, they rushed with one accord into the theatre.
verses.decoded: The whole city was thrown into chaos. They grabbed Gaius and Aristarchus, Paul's traveling companions from Macedonia, and all together rushed into the theater.

verses.kjv: And when Paul would have entered in unto the people, the disciples suffered him not.
verses.decoded: When Paul wanted to go into the crowd, his followers stopped him.

verses.kjv: And certain of the chief of Asia, which were his friends, sent unto him, desiring him that he would not adventure himself into the theatre.
verses.decoded: Some leading men of Asia, who were his friends, sent a message asking him not to risk going into the theater.

verses.kjv: Some therefore cried one thing, and some another: for the assembly was confused; and the more part knew not wherefore they were come together.
verses.decoded: Some people shouted different things, causing confusion, and most of the crowd didn’t even know why they had gathered.

verses.kjv: And they drew Alexander out of the multitude, the Jews putting him forward. And Alexander beckoned with the hand, and would have made his defence unto the people.
verses.decoded: They pulled a man named Alexander out of the crowd, pushed forward by the Jews. Alexander motioned to speak and tried to defend himself to the people.

verses.kjv: But when they knew that he was a Jew, all with one voice about the space of two hours cried out, Great is Diana of the Ephesians.
verses.decoded: But when the crowd realized he was a Jew, they shouted together for about two hours, "Great is Diana of the Ephesians!"

verses.kjv: And when the townclerk had appeased the people, he said, Ye men of Ephesus, what man is there that knoweth not how that the city of the Ephesians is a worshipper of the great goddess Diana, and of the image which fell down from Jupiter?
verses.decoded: After calming the crowd, the city official said, "Men of Ephesus, who doesn’t know that our city worships the great goddess Diana and the statue that fell from Jupiter?"

verses.kjv: Seeing then that these things cannot be spoken against, ye ought to be quiet, and to do nothing rashly.
verses.decoded: Since these things can’t be disputed, you should be calm and avoid acting impulsively.

verses.kjv: For ye have brought hither these men, which are neither robbers of churches, nor yet blasphemers of your goddess.
verses.decoded: You have brought here men who are neither thieves nor disrespecters of your goddess.

verses.kjv: Wherefore if Demetrius, and the craftsmen which are with him, have a matter against any man, the law is open, and there are deputies: let them implead one another.
verses.decoded: So if Demetrius and the craftsmen have a complaint against anyone, the courts are open and officials are here; they should take their case to court.

verses.kjv: But if ye enquire any thing concerning other matters, it shall be determined in a lawful assembly.
verses.decoded: If you want to discuss other issues, they should be handled in a regular, lawful meeting.

verses.kjv: For we are in danger to be called in question for this day’s uproar, there being no cause whereby we may give an account of this concourse.
verses.decoded: We risk being held responsible for today’s riot, since there is no valid reason for this gathering.

verses.kjv: And when he had thus spoken, he dismissed the assembly.
verses.decoded: After saying this, he dismissed the crowd.

verses.kjv: And after the uproar was ceased, Paul called unto him the disciples, and embraced them, and departed for to go into Macedonia.
verses.decoded: After the disturbance ended, Paul called the believers to him, hugged them, and left to go to Macedonia.

verses.kjv: And when he had gone over those parts, and had given them much exhortation, he came into Greece,
verses.decoded: After traveling through those regions and encouraging the believers there, he arrived in Greece.

verses.kjv: And there abode three months. And when the Jews laid wait for him, as he was about to sail into Syria, he purposed to return through Macedonia.
verses.decoded: He stayed there for three months. When some Jews planned to attack him as he was about to sail to Syria, he decided to go back through Macedonia instead.

verses.kjv: And there accompanied him into Asia Sopater of Berea; and of the Thessalonians, Aristarchus and Secundus; and Gaius of Derbe, and Timotheus; and of Asia, Tychicus and Trophimus.
verses.decoded: Sopater from Berea went with him to Asia, along with Aristarchus and Secundus from Thessalonica; Gaius from Derbe and Timothy; and Tychicus and Trophimus from Asia.

verses.kjv: These going before tarried for us at Troas.
verses.decoded: These men went ahead and waited for us at Troas.

verses.kjv: And we sailed away from Philippi after the days of unleavened bread, and came unto them to Troas in five days; where we abode seven days.
verses.decoded: We sailed from Philippi after the Passover week and reached Troas in five days, where we stayed for seven days.

verses.kjv: And upon the first day of the week, when the disciples came together to break bread, Paul preached unto them, ready to depart on the morrow; and continued his speech until midnight.
verses.decoded: On the first day of the week, when the believers gathered to share a meal, Paul preached to them, planning to leave the next day, and he spoke until midnight.

verses.kjv: And there were many lights in the upper chamber, where they were gathered together.
verses.decoded: There were many lamps lit in the upstairs room where they were meeting.

verses.kjv: And there sat in a window a certain young man named Eutychus, being fallen into a deep sleep: and as Paul was long preaching, he sunk down with sleep, and fell down from the third loft, and was taken up dead.
verses.decoded: A young man named Eutychus was sitting in a window and fell into a deep sleep while Paul was speaking for a long time. He fell from the third floor and was thought to be dead.

verses.kjv: And Paul went down, and fell on him, and embracing him said, Trouble not yourselves; for his life is in him.
verses.decoded: Paul went down, hugged him, and said, 'Don't worry, he is alive.'

verses.kjv: When he therefore was come up again, and had broken bread, and eaten, and talked a long while, even till break of day, so he departed.
verses.decoded: After Paul went back upstairs, broke bread, ate, and talked for a long time until dawn, he left.

verses.kjv: And they brought the young man alive, and were not a little comforted.
verses.decoded: They were very relieved to bring the young man back alive.

verses.kjv: And we went before to ship, and sailed unto Assos, there intending to take in Paul: for so had he appointed, minding himself to go afoot.
verses.decoded: We went ahead to the ship and sailed to Assos, planning to pick up Paul there because he had decided to walk on foot.

verses.kjv: And when he met with us at Assos, we took him in, and came to Mitylene.
verses.decoded: When Paul met us at Assos, we took him on board and sailed to Mitylene.

verses.kjv: And we sailed thence, and came the next day over against Chios; and the next day we arrived at Samos, and tarried at Trogyllium; and the next day we came to Miletus.
verses.decoded: We sailed from there and the next day reached the area opposite Chios; the following day we arrived at Samos and stayed at Trogyllium; the next day we reached Miletus.

verses.kjv: For Paul had determined to sail by Ephesus, because he would not spend the time in Asia: for he hasted, if it were possible for him, to be at Jerusalem the day of Pentecost.
verses.decoded: Paul decided to sail past Ephesus because he didn’t want to stay in the province of Asia. He was in a hurry, if possible, to reach Jerusalem by the day of Pentecost.

verses.kjv: And from Miletus he sent to Ephesus, and called the elders of the church.
verses.decoded: From Miletus, Paul sent a message to Ephesus asking the church leaders to come to him.

verses.kjv: And when they were come to him, he said unto them, Ye know, from the first day that I came into Asia, after what manner I have been with you at all seasons,
verses.decoded: When they arrived, Paul reminded them that from the very first day he came to Asia, they knew how he had lived among them at all times.

verses.kjv: Serving the LORD with all humility of mind, and with many tears, and temptations, which befell me by the lying in wait of the Jews:
verses.decoded: He served the Lord with complete humility, often crying and facing many challenges, including plots against him by some Jews.

verses.kjv: And how I kept back nothing that was profitable unto you, but have shewed you, and have taught you publickly, and from house to house,
verses.decoded: I did not hold back anything helpful; I taught you openly and also from house to house.

verses.kjv: Testifying both to the Jews, and also to the Greeks, repentance toward God, and faith toward our Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.decoded: I preached to both Jews and Greeks, urging them to turn to God in repentance and to have faith in our Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.kjv: And now, behold, I go bound in the spirit unto Jerusalem, not knowing the things that shall befall me there:
verses.decoded: Now I am compelled by the Spirit to go to Jerusalem, though I don’t know exactly what will happen to me there.

verses.kjv: Save that the Holy Ghost witnesseth in every city, saying that bonds and afflictions abide me.
verses.decoded: But the Holy Spirit warns me in every city that imprisonment and suffering are waiting for me.

verses.kjv: But none of these things move me, neither count I my life dear unto myself, so that I might finish my course with joy, and the ministry, which I have received of the Lord Jesus, to testify the gospel of the grace of God.
verses.decoded: None of this frightens me, and I don’t value my life so much that I won’t finish my mission with joy—the ministry God gave me to share the good news of His grace.

verses.kjv: And now, behold, I know that ye all, among whom I have gone preaching the kingdom of God, shall see my face no more.
verses.decoded: Now I am sure that none of you, among whom I have preached about God’s kingdom, will see me again.

verses.kjv: Wherefore I take you to record this day, that I am pure from the blood of all men.
verses.decoded: So today I declare before you all that I am innocent of anyone’s death or harm.

verses.kjv: For I have not shunned to declare unto you all the counsel of God.
verses.decoded: I have not hesitated to teach you everything God wanted me to share.

verses.kjv: Take heed therefore unto yourselves, and to all the flock, over the which the Holy Ghost hath made you overseers, to feed the church of God, which he hath purchased with his own blood.
verses.decoded: So be careful to watch over yourselves and all the believers, because the Holy Spirit appointed you as leaders to care for God’s church, which He bought with His own blood.

verses.kjv: For I know this, that after my departing shall grievous wolves enter in among you, not sparing the flock.
verses.decoded: I know that after I leave, harmful people will come among you and try to destroy the church.

verses.kjv: Also of your own selves shall men arise, speaking perverse things, to draw away disciples after them.
verses.decoded: Even some from your own group will rise up, teaching false ideas to lead followers away from the truth.

verses.kjv: Therefore watch, and remember, that by the space of three years I ceased not to warn every one night and day with tears.
verses.decoded: So be careful and remember that for three years I never stopped warning everyone, day and night, with tears.

verses.kjv: And now, brethren, I commend you to God, and to the word of his grace, which is able to build you up, and to give you an inheritance among all them which are sanctified.
verses.decoded: Now, brothers and sisters, I entrust you to God and to his message of grace, which can strengthen you and give you a place among all those made holy.

verses.kjv: I have coveted no man’s silver, or gold, or apparel.
verses.decoded: I have never wanted anyone’s silver, gold, or clothes.

verses.kjv: Yea, ye yourselves know, that these hands have ministered unto my necessities, and to them that were with me.
verses.decoded: You know yourselves that I worked with my own hands to provide for my needs and for those who were with me.

verses.kjv: I have shewed you all things, how that so labouring ye ought to support the weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, how he said, It is more blessed to give than to receive.
verses.decoded: I have taught you everything, showing that by working hard you should help the weak and remember what the Lord Jesus said: 'It is more blessed to give than to receive.'

verses.kjv: And when he had thus spoken, he kneeled down, and prayed with them all.
verses.decoded: After saying this, he knelt down and prayed with all of them.

verses.kjv: And they all wept sore, and fell on Paul’s neck, and kissed him,
verses.decoded: They all cried loudly, hugged Paul tightly, and kissed him,

verses.kjv: Sorrowing most of all for the words which he spake, that they should see his face no more. And they accompanied him unto the ship.
verses.decoded: Especially sad because of what he said—that they would never see his face again. Then they went with him to the ship.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, that after we were gotten from them, and had launched, we came with a straight course unto Coos, and the day following unto Rhodes, and from thence unto Patara:
verses.decoded: After we left them and set sail, we sailed straight to Coos, then the next day to Rhodes, and from there to Patara.

verses.kjv: And finding a ship sailing over unto Phenicia, we went aboard, and set forth.
verses.decoded: We found a ship going to Phoenicia, got on board, and set sail.

verses.kjv: Now when we had discovered Cyprus, we left it on the left hand, and sailed into Syria, and landed at Tyre: for there the ship was to unlade her burden.
verses.decoded: When we saw Cyprus, we kept it on our left and sailed into Syria, landing at Tyre because the ship was going to unload its cargo there.

verses.kjv: And finding disciples, we tarried there seven days: who said to Paul through the Spirit, that he should not go up to Jerusalem.
verses.decoded: We found some disciples and stayed there for seven days. They told Paul, through the Spirit, not to go to Jerusalem.

verses.kjv: And when we had accomplished those days, we departed and went our way; and they all brought us on our way, with wives and children, till we were out of the city: and we kneeled down on the shore, and prayed.
verses.decoded: After those days, we left. The people, including their wives and children, accompanied us out of the city. We knelt on the shore and prayed.

verses.kjv: And when we had taken our leave one of another, we took ship; and they returned home again.
verses.decoded: After saying goodbye to each other, we boarded the ship and they went back home.

verses.kjv: And when we had finished our course from Tyre, we came to Ptolemais, and saluted the brethren, and abode with them one day.
verses.decoded: After leaving Tyre, we arrived at Ptolemais, greeted the believers there, and stayed with them for one day.

verses.kjv: And the next day we that were of Paul’s company departed, and came unto Caesarea: and we entered into the house of Philip the evangelist, which was one of the seven; and abode with him.
verses.decoded: The next day, those of us traveling with Paul left and went to Caesarea. We stayed at the house of Philip the evangelist, one of the seven appointed leaders.

verses.kjv: And the same man had four daughters, virgins, which did prophesy.
verses.decoded: Philip had four unmarried daughters who had the gift of prophecy.

verses.kjv: And as we tarried there many days, there came down from Judaea a certain prophet, named Agabus.
verses.decoded: While we stayed there for several days, a prophet named Agabus came down from Judea.

verses.kjv: And when he was come unto us, he took Paul’s girdle, and bound his own hands and feet, and said, Thus saith the Holy Ghost, So shall the Jews at Jerusalem bind the man that owneth this girdle, and shall deliver him into the hands of the Gentiles.
verses.decoded: When he arrived, Agabus took Paul's belt, tied his own hands and feet with it, and said, 'The Holy Spirit says that the Jews in Jerusalem will bind the man who owns this belt and hand him over to the Gentiles.'

verses.kjv: And when we heard these things, both we, and they of that place, besought him not to go up to Jerusalem.
verses.decoded: When we heard this, both we and the local believers begged Paul not to go to Jerusalem.

verses.kjv: Then Paul answered, What mean ye to weep and to break mine heart? for I am ready not to be bound only, but also to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.
verses.decoded: Paul replied, 'Why are you crying and breaking my heart? I am ready not only to be arrested but also to die in Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.'

verses.kjv: And when he would not be persuaded, we ceased, saying, The will of the Lord be done.
verses.decoded: Since Paul would not be convinced otherwise, we stopped arguing and said, 'May the Lord’s will be done.'

verses.kjv: And after those days we took up our carriages, and went up to Jerusalem.
verses.decoded: After those days, we packed our belongings and went up to Jerusalem.

verses.kjv: There went with us also certain of the disciples of Caesarea, and brought with them one Mnason of Cyprus, an old disciple, with whom we should lodge.
verses.decoded: Some disciples from Caesarea went with us and brought along Mnason from Cyprus, an early believer, with whom we were to stay.

verses.kjv: And when we were come to Jerusalem, the brethren received us gladly.
verses.decoded: When we arrived in Jerusalem, the believers welcomed us warmly.

verses.kjv: And the day following Paul went in with us unto James; and all the elders were present.
verses.decoded: The next day Paul went with us to see James, and all the church leaders were there.

verses.kjv: And when he had saluted them, he declared particularly what things God had wrought among the Gentiles by his ministry.
verses.decoded: After greeting them, Paul explained in detail what God had done through his work among the Gentiles.

verses.kjv: And when they heard it, they glorified the Lord, and said unto him, Thou seest, brother, how many thousands of Jews there are which believe; and they are all zealous of the law:
verses.decoded: When they heard this, they praised the Lord and said, 'You see, brother, how many thousands of Jewish believers there are, and they are all very committed to the law.'

verses.kjv: And they are informed of thee, that thou teachest all the Jews which are among the Gentiles to forsake Moses, saying that they ought not to circumcise their children, neither to walk after the customs.
verses.decoded: They have heard that you teach all Jewish believers living among Gentiles to abandon Moses’ law, telling them not to circumcise their children or follow Jewish customs.

verses.kjv: What is it therefore? the multitude must needs come together: for they will hear that thou art come.
verses.decoded: So what should we do? A large crowd will gather when they hear you have arrived.

verses.kjv: Do therefore this that we say to thee: We have four men which have a vow on them;
verses.decoded: So do what we tell you: there are four men here under a vow;

verses.kjv: Them take, and purify thyself with them, and be at charges with them, that they may shave their heads: and all may know that those things, whereof they were informed concerning thee, are nothing; but that thou thyself also walkest orderly, and keepest the law.
verses.decoded: Join them in their purification rites and pay their expenses so they can shave their heads. This will show everyone that the rumors about you are false and that you yourself live properly and obey the law.

verses.kjv: As touching the Gentiles which believe, we have written and concluded that they observe no such thing, save only that they keep themselves from things offered to idols, and from blood, and from strangled, and from fornication.
verses.decoded: Regarding Gentile believers, we have decided and written that they do not need to follow these laws, except to avoid food sacrificed to idols, blood, meat from strangled animals, and sexual immorality.

verses.kjv: Then Paul took the men, and the next day purifying himself with them entered into the temple, to signify the accomplishment of the days of purification, until that an offering should be offered for every one of them.
verses.decoded: Paul took the men, and the next day he purified himself along with them and entered the temple to show that the days of purification were complete, until the offering for each of them was made.

verses.kjv: And when the seven days were almost ended, the Jews which were of Asia, when they saw him in the temple, stirred up all the people, and laid hands on him,
verses.decoded: As the seven days were nearly over, some Jews from Asia saw Paul in the temple, stirred up the crowd, and grabbed him.

verses.kjv: Crying out, Men of Israel, help: This is the man, that teacheth all men every where against the people, and the law, and this place: and further brought Greeks also into the temple, and hath polluted this holy place.
verses.decoded: They shouted, 'Men of Israel, help! This is the man who teaches everyone everywhere against our people, the law, and this place. He even brought Greeks into the temple and defiled this holy place.'

verses.kjv: (For they had seen before with him in the city Trophimus an Ephesian, whom they supposed that Paul had brought into the temple.)
verses.decoded: (They had previously seen Paul with Trophimus, an Ephesian, in the city and assumed Paul had brought him into the temple.)

verses.kjv: And all the city was moved, and the people ran together: and they took Paul, and drew him out of the temple: and forthwith the doors were shut.
verses.decoded: The whole city was stirred up, and a crowd gathered. They seized Paul and dragged him out of the temple, then immediately shut the doors.

verses.kjv: And as they went about to kill him, tidings came unto the chief captain of the band, that all Jerusalem was in an uproar.
verses.decoded: As they were trying to kill him, news reached the commander of the soldiers that the whole city of Jerusalem was in chaos.

verses.kjv: Who immediately took soldiers and centurions, and ran down unto them: and when they saw the chief captain and the soldiers, they left beating of Paul.
verses.decoded: The commander quickly took some soldiers and officers and ran to the crowd. When the people saw the commander and the soldiers, they stopped beating Paul.

verses.kjv: Then the chief captain came near, and took him, and commanded him to be bound with two chains; and demanded who he was, and what he had done.
verses.decoded: The commander came close, arrested Paul, ordered him to be chained with two chains, and asked who he was and what he had done.

verses.kjv: And some cried one thing, some another, among the multitude: and when he could not know the certainty for the tumult, he commanded him to be carried into the castle.
verses.decoded: The crowd shouted different things, making it impossible for the commander to understand what was happening, so he ordered Paul to be taken into the fortress.

verses.kjv: And when he came upon the stairs, so it was, that he was borne of the soldiers for the violence of the people.
verses.decoded: As Paul reached the stairs, the soldiers had to carry him because the crowd was so violent.

verses.kjv: For the multitude of the people followed after, crying, Away with him.
verses.decoded: The crowd followed, shouting, 'Get rid of him!'

verses.kjv: And as Paul was to be led into the castle, he said unto the chief captain, May I speak unto thee? Who said, Canst thou speak Greek?
verses.decoded: As Paul was being taken into the fortress, he asked the commander, 'May I say something to you?' The commander replied, 'Do you speak Greek?'

verses.kjv: Art not thou that Egyptian, which before these days madest an uproar, and leddest out into the wilderness four thousand men that were murderers?
verses.decoded: The commander asked, 'Aren't you the Egyptian who recently caused a riot and led about four thousand violent men into the wilderness?'

verses.kjv: But Paul said, I am a man which am a Jew of Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, a citizen of no mean city: and, I beseech thee, suffer me to speak unto the people.
verses.decoded: Paul replied, 'I am a Jew from Tarsus in Cilicia, a city of some importance. Please allow me to speak to the people.'

verses.kjv: And when he had given him licence, Paul stood on the stairs, and beckoned with the hand unto the people. And when there was made a great silence, he spake unto them in the Hebrew tongue, saying,
verses.decoded: After the commander gave permission, Paul stood on the steps, signaled to the crowd, and when they became quiet, he spoke to them in Hebrew.

verses.kjv: Men, brethren, and fathers, hear ye my defence which I make now unto you.
verses.decoded: Men, brothers, and fathers, listen to my defense that I am making to you now.

verses.kjv: (And when they heard that he spake in the Hebrew tongue to them, they kept the more silence: and he saith,)
verses.decoded: When they heard that he was speaking to them in Hebrew, they became even more silent. Then he said,

verses.kjv: I am verily a man which am a Jew, born in Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, yet brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel, and taught according to the perfect manner of the law of the fathers, and was zealous toward God, as ye all are this day.
verses.decoded: I am truly a Jew, born in Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, but I was raised here in Jerusalem and educated under Gamaliel, taught strictly according to our ancestral law. I was very zealous for God, just as you all are now.

verses.kjv: And I persecuted this way unto the death, binding and delivering into prisons both men and women.
verses.decoded: I persecuted the followers of this way to the death, arresting both men and women and putting them in prison.

verses.kjv: As also the high priest doth bear me witness, and all the estate of the elders: from whom also I received letters unto the brethren, and went to Damascus, to bring them which were there bound unto Jerusalem, for to be punished.
verses.decoded: The high priest and the elders can confirm this. I even received letters from them to take to the brothers in Damascus, so I could arrest those there and bring them back to Jerusalem for punishment.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, that, as I made my journey, and was come nigh unto Damascus about noon, suddenly there shone from heaven a great light round about me.
verses.decoded: As I was traveling and got near Damascus around noon, suddenly a bright light from heaven shone all around me.

verses.kjv: And I fell unto the ground, and heard a voice saying unto me, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?
verses.decoded: I fell to the ground and heard a voice saying to me, 'Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?'

verses.kjv: And I answered, Who art thou, Lord? And he said unto me, I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom thou persecutest.
verses.decoded: I asked, 'Who are you, Lord?' He said, 'I am Jesus of Nazareth, the one you are persecuting.'

verses.kjv: And they that were with me saw indeed the light, and were afraid; but they heard not the voice of him that spake to me.
verses.decoded: Those traveling with me saw the light and were afraid, but they did not hear the voice speaking to me.

verses.kjv: And I said, What shall I do, LORD? And the Lord said unto me, Arise, and go into Damascus; and there it shall be told thee of all things which are appointed for thee to do.
verses.decoded: I asked, 'What should I do, Lord?' The Lord told me, 'Get up and go into Damascus, where you will be told what you must do.'

verses.kjv: And when I could not see for the glory of that light, being led by the hand of them that were with me, I came into Damascus.
verses.decoded: Because the brightness of the light blinded me, my companions led me by the hand into Damascus.

verses.kjv: And one Ananias, a devout man according to the law, having a good report of all the Jews which dwelt there,
verses.decoded: There was a man named Ananias, a devout follower of the law, well respected by all the Jews living there.

verses.kjv: Came unto me, and stood, and said unto me, Brother Saul, receive thy sight. And the same hour I looked up upon him.
verses.decoded: Ananias came to me, stood beside me, and said, 'Brother Saul, regain your sight.' Immediately, I was able to see him.

verses.kjv: And he said, The God of our fathers hath chosen thee, that thou shouldest know his will, and see that Just One, and shouldest hear the voice of his mouth.
verses.decoded: He told me, 'The God of our ancestors has chosen you so that you will know His will, see the Righteous One, and hear His voice.'

verses.kjv: For thou shalt be his witness unto all men of what thou hast seen and heard.
verses.decoded: You will be His witness to everyone of what you have seen and heard.

verses.kjv: And now why tarriest thou? arise, and be baptized, and wash away thy sins, calling on the name of the Lord.
verses.decoded: So why are you waiting? Get up, be baptized, and wash away your sins by calling on the Lord's name.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, that, when I was come again to Jerusalem, even while I prayed in the temple, I was in a trance;
verses.decoded: When I returned to Jerusalem and was praying in the temple, I fell into a trance.

verses.kjv: And saw him saying unto me, Make haste, and get thee quickly out of Jerusalem: for they will not receive thy testimony concerning me.
verses.decoded: I saw him say to me, 'Hurry and leave Jerusalem quickly, because the people there will not accept your testimony about me.'

verses.kjv: And I said, Lord, they know that I imprisoned and beat in every synagogue them that believed on thee:
verses.decoded: I answered, 'Lord, they know that I have imprisoned and beaten those who believe in you in every synagogue.'

verses.kjv: And when the blood of thy martyr Stephen was shed, I also was standing by, and consenting unto his death, and kept the raiment of them that slew him.
verses.decoded: When Stephen was killed, I was there, agreed with his death, and guarded the clothes of those who killed him.

verses.kjv: And he said unto me, Depart: for I will send thee far hence unto the Gentiles.
verses.decoded: Then he said to me, 'Go away, because I am sending you far away to the Gentiles.'

verses.kjv: And they gave him audience unto this word, and then lifted up their voices, and said, Away with such a fellow from the earth: for it is not fit that he should live.
verses.decoded: They listened to him until this point, then shouted, 'Get rid of this man! He shouldn’t be allowed to live!'

verses.kjv: And as they cried out, and cast off their clothes, and threw dust into the air,
verses.decoded: As they shouted, they tore off their clothes and threw dust into the air.

verses.kjv: The chief captain commanded him to be brought into the castle, and bade that he should be examined by scourging; that he might know wherefore they cried so against him.
verses.decoded: The commander ordered Paul to be taken to the barracks and whipped to find out why the crowd was shouting against him.

verses.kjv: And as they bound him with thongs, Paul said unto the centurion that stood by, Is it lawful for you to scourge a man that is a Roman, and uncondemned?
verses.decoded: When they were tying him up, Paul asked the officer, 'Is it legal for you to whip a Roman citizen who hasn’t been found guilty?'

verses.kjv: When the centurion heard that, he went and told the chief captain, saying, Take heed what thou doest: for this man is a Roman.
verses.decoded: The officer told the commander, 'Be careful what you do, because this man is a Roman citizen.'

verses.kjv: Then the chief captain came, and said unto him, Tell me, art thou a Roman? He said, Yea.
verses.decoded: The commander came and asked Paul, 'Are you a Roman citizen?' He replied, 'Yes.'

verses.kjv: And the chief captain answered, With a great sum obtained I this freedom. And Paul said, But I was free born.
verses.decoded: The commander said, 'I bought my citizenship for a large amount of money.' Paul replied, 'I was born a citizen.'

verses.kjv: Then straightway they departed from him which should have examined him: and the chief captain also was afraid, after he knew that he was a Roman, and because he had bound him.
verses.decoded: Immediately, those who were going to question him stopped, and the commander was afraid because he had arrested a Roman citizen.

verses.kjv: On the morrow, because he would have known the certainty wherefore he was accused of the Jews, he loosed him from his bands, and commanded the chief priests and all their council to appear, and brought Paul down, and set him before them.
verses.decoded: The next day, wanting to understand the Jewish charges against Paul, the commander released him from his chains and ordered the Jewish leaders to come. Then he brought Paul before them.

verses.kjv: And Paul, earnestly beholding the council, said, Men and brethren, I have lived in all good conscience before God until this day.
verses.decoded: Paul looked closely at the council and said, "Men and brothers, I have lived with a clear conscience before God up to this day."

verses.kjv: And the high priest Ananias commanded them that stood by him to smite him on the mouth.
verses.decoded: The high priest Ananias ordered those standing near him to slap Paul in the mouth.

verses.kjv: Then said Paul unto him, God shall smite thee, thou whited wall: for sittest thou to judge me after the law, and commandest me to be smitten contrary to the law?
verses.decoded: Paul replied, "God will strike you, you whitewashed wall! Are you sitting to judge me by the law, yet you order me to be hit against the law?"

verses.kjv: And they that stood by said, Revilest thou God’s high priest?
verses.decoded: Those standing nearby said, "Are you insulting God's high priest?"

verses.kjv: Then said Paul, I wist not, brethren, that he was the high priest: for it is written, Thou shalt not speak evil of the ruler of thy people.
verses.decoded: Paul answered, "Brothers, I did not realize he was the high priest, because it is written, 'Do not speak evil about the ruler of your people.'"

verses.kjv: But when Paul perceived that the one part were Sadducees, and the other Pharisees, he cried out in the council, Men and brethren, I am a Pharisee, the son of a Pharisee: of the hope and resurrection of the dead I am called in question.
verses.decoded: When Paul noticed that some were Sadducees and others Pharisees, he shouted, "Men and brothers, I am a Pharisee, the son of a Pharisee. I am being judged because of my hope in the resurrection of the dead."

verses.kjv: And when he had so said, there arose a dissension between the Pharisees and the Sadducees: and the multitude was divided.
verses.decoded: After he said this, a dispute broke out between the Pharisees and Sadducees, and the crowd was divided.

verses.kjv: For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, neither angel, nor spirit: but the Pharisees confess both.
verses.decoded: The Sadducees say there is no resurrection, no angels, and no spirits, but the Pharisees believe in all these.

verses.kjv: And there arose a great cry: and the scribes that were of the Pharisees’ part arose, and strove, saying, We find no evil in this man: but if a spirit or an angel hath spoken to him, let us not fight against God.
verses.decoded: A loud argument started, and the Pharisee scribes stood up and said, "We find nothing wrong with this man. But if a spirit or angel has spoken to him, we should not oppose God."

verses.kjv: And when there arose a great dissension, the chief captain, fearing lest Paul should have been pulled in pieces of them, commanded the soldiers to go down, and to take him by force from among them, and to bring him into the castle.
verses.decoded: When the argument became violent, the commander feared the crowd would tear Paul apart, so he ordered soldiers to forcefully remove Paul and bring him into the fortress.

verses.kjv: And the night following the Lord stood by him, and said, Be of good cheer, Paul: for as thou hast testified of me in Jerusalem, so must thou bear witness also at Rome.
verses.decoded: That night, the Lord stood beside Paul and said, "Be encouraged, Paul. Just as you have testified about me in Jerusalem, you must also testify in Rome."

verses.kjv: And when it was day, certain of the Jews banded together, and bound themselves under a curse, saying that they would neither eat nor drink till they had killed Paul.
verses.decoded: The next day, some Jews formed a conspiracy, taking an oath not to eat or drink until they had killed Paul.

verses.kjv: And they were more than forty which had made this conspiracy.
verses.decoded: More than forty people joined this conspiracy.

verses.kjv: And they came to the chief priests and elders, and said, We have bound ourselves under a great curse, that we will eat nothing until we have slain Paul.
verses.decoded: They went to the chief priests and elders and said, "We have taken a solemn oath not to eat until we have killed Paul."

verses.kjv: Now therefore ye with the council signify to the chief captain that he bring him down unto you to morrow, as though ye would enquire something more perfectly concerning him: and we, or ever he come near, are ready to kill him.
verses.decoded: So you, along with the council, tell the commander to bring Paul to you tomorrow as if you want to question him more thoroughly. But before he arrives, we will be ready to kill him.

verses.kjv: And when Paul’s sister’s son heard of their lying in wait, he went and entered into the castle, and told Paul.
verses.decoded: When Paul's nephew heard about the plot against him, he went into the fortress and warned Paul.

verses.kjv: Then Paul called one of the centurions unto him, and said, Bring this young man unto the chief captain: for he hath a certain thing to tell him.
verses.decoded: Paul called a soldier and said, 'Take this young man to the commander because he has something important to tell him.'

verses.kjv: So he took him, and brought him to the chief captain, and said, Paul the prisoner called me unto him, and prayed me to bring this young man unto thee, who hath something to say unto thee.
verses.decoded: The soldier took the young man to the commander and explained that Paul had asked him to bring the young man because he had something to say.

verses.kjv: Then the chief captain took him by the hand, and went with him aside privately, and asked him, What is that thou hast to tell me?
verses.decoded: The commander took the young man aside privately and asked, 'What do you want to tell me?'

verses.kjv: And he said, The Jews have agreed to desire thee that thou wouldest bring down Paul to morrow into the council, as though they would enquire somewhat of him more perfectly.
verses.decoded: The young man said, 'The Jewish leaders have planned to ask you to bring Paul before the council tomorrow, pretending they want to question him more thoroughly.'

verses.kjv: But do not thou yield unto them: for there lie in wait for him of them more than forty men, which have bound themselves with an oath, that they will neither eat nor drink till they have killed him: and now are they ready, looking for a promise from thee.
verses.decoded: But don't agree to it, because over forty men have sworn an oath not to eat or drink until they kill Paul. They are waiting for your approval.

verses.kjv: So the chief captain then let the young man depart, and charged him, See thou tell no man that thou hast shewed these things to me.
verses.decoded: The commander let the young man go and told him not to tell anyone that he had shared this information.

verses.kjv: And he called unto him two centurions, saying, Make ready two hundred soldiers to go to Caesarea, and horsemen threescore and ten, and spearmen two hundred, at the third hour of the night;
verses.decoded: He called two officers and ordered them to prepare 200 soldiers, 70 cavalry, and 200 spearmen to leave at 9 PM to go to Caesarea.

verses.kjv: And provide them beasts, that they may set Paul on, and bring him safe unto Felix the governor.
verses.decoded: He also told them to get animals to carry Paul safely to Governor Felix.

verses.kjv: And he wrote a letter after this manner:
verses.decoded: Then he wrote a letter that said:

verses.kjv: Claudius Lysias unto the most excellent governor Felix sendeth greeting.
verses.decoded: Claudius Lysias sends greetings to the honorable Governor Felix.

verses.kjv: This man was taken of the Jews, and should have been killed of them: then came I with an army, and rescued him, having understood that he was a Roman.
verses.decoded: This man was seized by the Jews and was about to be killed, but I arrived with soldiers and saved him because I learned he was a Roman citizen.

verses.kjv: And when I would have known the cause wherefore they accused him, I brought him forth into their council:
verses.decoded: When I wanted to find out why they were accusing him, I brought him before their council.

verses.kjv: Whom I perceived to be accused of questions of their law, but to have nothing laid to his charge worthy of death or of bonds.
verses.decoded: I saw that he was being accused only about their law and that there was no charge against him deserving death or imprisonment.

verses.kjv: And when it was told me how that the Jews laid wait for the man, I sent straightway to thee, and gave commandment to his accusers also to say before thee what they had against him. Farewell.
verses.decoded: When I learned that the Jews were planning to ambush him, I immediately sent him to you and ordered his accusers to present their case before you. Goodbye.

verses.kjv: Then the soldiers, as it was commanded them, took Paul, and brought him by night to Antipatris.
verses.decoded: The soldiers followed their orders and took Paul, bringing him at night to Antipatris.

verses.kjv: On the morrow they left the horsemen to go with him, and returned to the castle:
verses.decoded: The next day, they left some cavalry to accompany Paul and then returned to the fortress.

verses.kjv: Who, when they came to Caesarea, and delivered the epistle to the governor, presented Paul also before him.
verses.decoded: When they reached Caesarea, they gave the letter to the governor and also brought Paul before him.

verses.kjv: And when the governor had read the letter, he asked of what province he was. And when he understood that he was of Cilicia;
verses.decoded: After reading the letter, the governor asked where Paul was from. When he learned Paul was from Cilicia,

verses.kjv: I will hear thee, said he, when thine accusers are also come. And he commanded him to be kept in Herod’s judgment hall.
verses.decoded: he said, 'I will listen to you when your accusers arrive.' Then he ordered Paul to be kept in Herod's palace prison.

verses.kjv: And after five days Ananias the high priest descended with the elders, and with a certain orator named Tertullus, who informed the governor against Paul.
verses.decoded: After five days, the high priest Ananias came down with the elders and a lawyer named Tertullus, who presented charges against Paul to the governor.

verses.kjv: And when he was called forth, Tertullus began to accuse him, saying, Seeing that by thee we enjoy great quietness, and that very worthy deeds are done unto this nation by thy providence,
verses.decoded: When Paul was called forward, Tertullus began his accusation, saying, 'Because of you we have peace and good government, and you do many good things for this nation,'

verses.kjv: We accept it always, and in all places, most noble Felix, with all thankfulness.
verses.decoded: We always and everywhere appreciate this, most honorable Felix, and we thank you for it.

verses.kjv: Notwithstanding, that I be not further tedious unto thee, I pray thee that thou wouldest hear us of thy clemency a few words.
verses.decoded: But so I don’t take up too much of your time, I ask that you kindly listen to a few words from us.

verses.kjv: For we have found this man a pestilent fellow, and a mover of sedition among all the Jews throughout the world, and a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes:
verses.decoded: We have found this man to be a troublemaker, stirring up riots among Jews everywhere, and he is the leader of the Nazarene sect.

verses.kjv: Who also hath gone about to profane the temple: whom we took, and would have judged according to our law.
verses.decoded: He even tried to desecrate the temple, so we arrested him and wanted to judge him by our law.

verses.kjv: But the chief captain Lysias came upon us, and with great violence took him away out of our hands,
verses.decoded: But the commander Lysias came with force and took him away from us by violence.

verses.kjv: Commanding his accusers to come unto thee: by examining of whom thyself mayest take knowledge of all these things, whereof we accuse him.
verses.decoded: He ordered his accusers to bring their case before you, so you can investigate these charges yourself.

verses.kjv: And the Jews also assented, saying that these things were so.
verses.decoded: The Jews agreed and confirmed that these things were true.

verses.kjv: Then Paul, after that the governor had beckoned unto him to speak, answered, Forasmuch as I know that thou hast been of many years a judge unto this nation, I do the more cheerfully answer for myself:
verses.decoded: Then Paul, after the governor signaled him to speak, said, 'Since you have been a judge over this nation for many years, I am glad to defend myself before you.'

verses.kjv: Because that thou mayest understand, that there are yet but twelve days since I went up to Jerusalem for to worship.
verses.decoded: So you know, it has only been twelve days since I went up to Jerusalem to worship.

verses.kjv: And they neither found me in the temple disputing with any man, neither raising up the people, neither in the synagogues, nor in the city:
verses.decoded: They did not find me arguing with anyone in the temple, stirring up the crowd, in the synagogues, or anywhere in the city.

verses.kjv: Neither can they prove the things whereof they now accuse me.
verses.decoded: And they cannot prove the charges they are now making against me.

verses.kjv: But this I confess unto thee, that after the way which they call heresy, so worship I the God of my fathers, believing all things which are written in the law and in the prophets:
verses.decoded: But I admit to you that I worship the God of my ancestors in the way they call a sect, believing everything written in the Law and the Prophets.

verses.kjv: And have hope toward God, which they themselves also allow, that there shall be a resurrection of the dead, both of the just and unjust.
verses.decoded: I have hope in God, which they themselves accept, that there will be a resurrection of both the righteous and the wicked.

verses.kjv: And herein do I exercise myself, to have always a conscience void of offence toward God, and toward men.
verses.decoded: I always try to live with a clear conscience, both before God and before people.

verses.kjv: Now after many years I came to bring alms to my nation, and offerings.
verses.decoded: After many years, I came to bring gifts and offerings to my people.

verses.kjv: Whereupon certain Jews from Asia found me purified in the temple, neither with multitude, nor with tumult.
verses.decoded: Some Jews from Asia saw me in the temple, purified and peaceful, without any crowd or disturbance.

verses.kjv: Who ought to have been here before thee, and object, if they had ought against me.
verses.decoded: If they had anything against me, they should be here to accuse me now.

verses.kjv: Or else let these same here say, if they have found any evil doing in me, while I stood before the council,
verses.decoded: Or let these men say if they found me guilty of any wrongdoing when I stood before the Jewish council.

verses.kjv: Except it be for this one voice, that I cried standing among them, Touching the resurrection of the dead I am called in question by you this day.
verses.decoded: Except for this one thing: I was arguing about the resurrection of the dead, and that’s why you are accusing me today.

verses.kjv: And when Felix heard these things, having more perfect knowledge of that way, he deferred them, and said, When Lysias the chief captain shall come down, I will know the uttermost of your matter.
verses.decoded: When Felix heard this, and knew more about this teaching, he postponed the case and said, 'When Captain Lysias arrives, I will learn all the facts.'

verses.kjv: And he commanded a centurion to keep Paul, and to let him have liberty, and that he should forbid none of his acquaintance to minister or come unto him.
verses.decoded: He ordered a soldier to guard Paul but to give him freedom and allow his friends to visit and help him.

verses.kjv: And after certain days, when Felix came with his wife Drusilla, which was a Jewess, he sent for Paul, and heard him concerning the faith in Christ.
verses.decoded: After some days, Felix came with his wife Drusilla, who was Jewish, and sent for Paul to hear about faith in Christ.

verses.kjv: And as he reasoned of righteousness, temperance, and judgment to come, Felix trembled, and answered, Go thy way for this time; when I have a convenient season, I will call for thee.
verses.decoded: As Paul talked about right living, self-control, and the coming judgment, Felix was afraid and said, 'Go for now; when it’s a good time, I will call for you.'

verses.kjv: He hoped also that money should have been given him of Paul, that he might loose him: wherefore he sent for him the oftener, and communed with him.
verses.decoded: Felix hoped Paul would give him money to secure his release, so he often sent for Paul and talked with him.

verses.kjv: But after two years Porcius Festus came into Felix’ room: and Felix, willing to shew the Jews a pleasure, left Paul bound.
verses.decoded: After two years, Porcius Festus replaced Felix, and Felix, wanting to please the Jews, left Paul imprisoned.

verses.kjv: Now when Festus was come into the province, after three days he ascended from Caesarea to Jerusalem.
verses.decoded: When Festus arrived in the province, after three days he went up from Caesarea to Jerusalem.

verses.kjv: Then the high priest and the chief of the Jews informed him against Paul, and besought him,
verses.decoded: The high priest and leading Jewish officials brought accusations against Paul and asked Festus for help.

verses.kjv: And desired favour against him, that he would send for him to Jerusalem, laying wait in the way to kill him.
verses.decoded: They requested that Festus send Paul to Jerusalem, where they planned to ambush and kill him on the way.

verses.kjv: But Festus answered, that Paul should be kept at Caesarea, and that he himself would depart shortly thither.
verses.decoded: But Festus replied that Paul should stay in Caesarea, and that he himself would soon return there.

verses.kjv: Let them therefore, said he, which among you are able, go down with me, and accuse this man, if there be any wickedness in him.
verses.decoded: He said, 'Let those who can come down with me and bring charges against this man if he has done anything wrong.'

verses.kjv: And when he had tarried among them more than ten days, he went down unto Caesarea; and the next day sitting on the judgment seat commanded Paul to be brought.
verses.decoded: After staying with them for more than ten days, Festus went down to Caesarea. The next day, while sitting as judge, he ordered Paul to be brought before him.

verses.kjv: And when he was come, the Jews which came down from Jerusalem stood round about, and laid many and grievous complaints against Paul, which they could not prove.
verses.decoded: When Paul arrived, the Jews who had come from Jerusalem surrounded him and made many serious accusations, but they could not prove any of them.

verses.kjv: While he answered for himself, Neither against the law of the Jews, neither against the temple, nor yet against Caesar, have I offended any thing at all.
verses.decoded: Paul defended himself by saying, 'I have done nothing wrong against Jewish law, the temple, or Caesar.'

verses.kjv: But Festus, willing to do the Jews a pleasure, answered Paul, and said, Wilt thou go up to Jerusalem, and there be judged of these things before me?
verses.decoded: But Festus, wanting to please the Jews, said to Paul, 'Do you want to go to Jerusalem and be tried there for these charges before me?'

verses.kjv: Then said Paul, I stand at Caesar’s judgment seat, where I ought to be judged: to the Jews have I done no wrong, as thou very well knowest.
verses.decoded: Paul replied, 'I am standing before Caesar’s court, where I should be tried. I have done nothing wrong to the Jews, as you know very well.'

verses.kjv: For if I be an offender, or have committed any thing worthy of death, I refuse not to die: but if there be none of these things whereof these accuse me, no man may deliver me unto them. I appeal unto Caesar.
