verses.decoded: Paul said, 'If I have done anything wrong or deserve death, I am not refusing to die. But if there is no truth in these accusations, no one can hand me over to them. I appeal to Caesar.'

verses.kjv: Then Festus, when he had conferred with the council, answered, Hast thou appealed unto Caesar? unto Caesar shalt thou go.
verses.decoded: After consulting with his advisors, Festus said, 'You have appealed to Caesar, so you will go to Caesar.'

verses.kjv: And after certain days king Agrippa and Bernice came unto Caesarea to salute Festus.
verses.decoded: A few days later, King Agrippa and Bernice came to Caesarea to greet Festus.

verses.kjv: And when they had been there many days, Festus declared Paul’s cause unto the king, saying, There is a certain man left in bonds by Felix:
verses.decoded: After staying several days, Festus explained Paul's case to the king, saying, 'There is a man whom Felix left in prison.'

verses.kjv: About whom, when I was at Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jews informed me, desiring to have judgment against him.
verses.decoded: When I was in Jerusalem, the chief priests and Jewish elders told me about him and wanted a judgment against him.

verses.kjv: To whom I answered, It is not the manner of the Romans to deliver any man to die, before that he which is accused have the accusers face to face, and have licence to answer for himself concerning the crime laid against him.
verses.decoded: I replied that it is not the Roman way to hand over someone to be executed before the accused has faced their accusers and been allowed to defend themselves against the charges.

verses.kjv: Therefore, when they were come hither, without any delay on the morrow I sat on the judgment seat, and commanded the man to be brought forth.
verses.decoded: So when they arrived, the next day without delay I took my seat as judge and ordered the man to be brought before me.

verses.kjv: Against whom when the accusers stood up, they brought none accusation of such things as I supposed:
verses.decoded: When the accusers stood up, they did not bring charges about the things I expected.

verses.kjv: But had certain questions against him of their own superstition, and of one Jesus, which was dead, whom Paul affirmed to be alive.
verses.decoded: Instead, they had some questions about their own religious beliefs and about Jesus, who died but whom Paul claimed was alive.

verses.kjv: And because I doubted of such manner of questions, I asked him whether he would go to Jerusalem, and there be judged of these matters.
verses.decoded: Since I was unsure how to handle these questions, I asked Paul if he was willing to go to Jerusalem to be tried on these matters.

verses.kjv: But when Paul had appealed to be reserved unto the hearing of Augustus, I commanded him to be kept till I might send him to Caesar.
verses.decoded: But Paul appealed to have his case heard by Caesar, so I ordered that he be kept in custody until I could send him to Caesar.

verses.kjv: Then Agrippa said unto Festus, I would also hear the man myself. To morrow, said he, thou shalt hear him.
verses.decoded: Then Agrippa told Festus, 'I would like to hear this man myself.' Festus replied, 'Tomorrow you will hear him.'

verses.kjv: And on the morrow, when Agrippa was come, and Bernice, with great pomp, and was entered into the place of hearing, with the chief captains, and principal men of the city, at Festus’ commandment Paul was brought forth.
verses.decoded: The next day, Agrippa and Bernice arrived with great ceremony and entered the courtroom along with the leading military officers and important city officials. At Festus' order, Paul was brought out.

verses.kjv: And Festus said, King Agrippa, and all men which are here present with us, ye see this man, about whom all the multitude of the Jews have dealt with me, both at Jerusalem, and also here, crying that he ought not to live any longer.
verses.decoded: Festus said, 'King Agrippa and everyone here, you see this man. The Jewish crowd has complained about him to me both in Jerusalem and here, shouting that he should be put to death.'

verses.kjv: But when I found that he had committed nothing worthy of death, and that he himself hath appealed to Augustus, I have determined to send him.
verses.decoded: But I found that he had done nothing deserving death, and since he appealed to Caesar, I have decided to send him there.

verses.kjv: Of whom I have no certain thing to write unto my lord. Wherefore I have brought him forth before you, and specially before thee, O king Agrippa, that, after examination had, I might have somewhat to write.
verses.decoded: I have nothing definite to report to my superior about him. So I brought him before you, especially you King Agrippa, hoping that after your examination I will have something to write.

verses.kjv: For it seemeth to me unreasonable to send a prisoner, and not withal to signify the crimes laid against him.
verses.decoded: It seems unreasonable to me to send a prisoner without also explaining the charges against him.

verses.kjv: Then Agrippa said unto Paul, Thou art permitted to speak for thyself. Then Paul stretched forth the hand, and answered for himself:
verses.decoded: Then Agrippa said to Paul, 'You are allowed to speak for yourself.' So Paul raised his hand and began to speak.

verses.kjv: I think myself happy, king Agrippa, because I shall answer for myself this day before thee touching all the things whereof I am accused of the Jews:
verses.decoded: I consider myself fortunate, King Agrippa, because today I get to defend myself before you regarding all the accusations the Jews have made against me.

verses.kjv: Especially because I know thee to be expert in all customs and questions which are among the Jews: wherefore I beseech thee to hear me patiently.
verses.decoded: Especially since I know you are well informed about Jewish customs and controversies, I ask you to listen to me carefully.

verses.kjv: My manner of life from my youth, which was at the first among mine own nation at Jerusalem, know all the Jews;
verses.decoded: All the Jews know how I lived from my youth, first in my own nation in Jerusalem.

verses.kjv: Which knew me from the beginning, if they would testify, that after the most straitest sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee.
verses.decoded: Those who have known me from the start can confirm that I lived as a Pharisee, following the strictest sect of our religion.

verses.kjv: And now I stand and am judged for the hope of the promise made of God unto our fathers:
verses.decoded: Now I am here, being judged because of the hope in the promise God made to our ancestors.

verses.kjv: Unto which promise our twelve tribes, instantly serving God day and night, hope to come. For which hope’s sake, king Agrippa, I am accused of the Jews.
verses.decoded: Our twelve tribes eagerly serve God day and night, hoping to receive this promise. It is because of this hope, King Agrippa, that the Jews accuse me.

verses.kjv: Why should it be thought a thing incredible with you, that God should raise the dead?
verses.decoded: Why do you find it hard to believe that God can raise the dead?

verses.kjv: I verily thought with myself, that I ought to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus of Nazareth.
verses.decoded: I honestly thought to myself that I should do many things against the followers of Jesus of Nazareth.

verses.kjv: Which thing I also did in Jerusalem: and many of the saints did I shut up in prison, having received authority from the chief priests; and when they were put to death, I gave my voice against them.
verses.decoded: I did these things in Jerusalem: I imprisoned many believers with authority from the chief priests, and when some were killed, I agreed with it.

verses.kjv: And I punished them oft in every synagogue, and compelled them to blaspheme; and being exceedingly mad against them, I persecuted them even unto strange cities.
verses.decoded: I often punished them in every synagogue, forcing them to speak against their faith. I was extremely angry and persecuted them even in foreign cities.

verses.kjv: Whereupon as I went to Damascus with authority and commission from the chief priests,
verses.decoded: So, as I was going to Damascus with authority and orders from the chief priests,

verses.kjv: At midday, O king, I saw in the way a light from heaven, above the brightness of the sun, shining round about me and them which journeyed with me.
verses.decoded: At noon, King Agrippa, I saw a light from heaven, brighter than the sun, shining around me and those traveling with me.

verses.kjv: And when we were all fallen to the earth, I heard a voice speaking unto me, and saying in the Hebrew tongue, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me? it is hard for thee to kick against the pricks.
verses.decoded: We all fell to the ground, and I heard a voice speaking to me in Hebrew: 'Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me? It is hard for you to fight against this.'

verses.kjv: And I said, Who art thou, Lord? And he said, I am Jesus whom thou persecutest.
verses.decoded: I asked, 'Who are you, Lord?' He replied, 'I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.'

verses.kjv: But rise, and stand upon thy feet: for I have appeared unto thee for this purpose, to make thee a minister and a witness both of these things which thou hast seen, and of those things in the which I will appear unto thee;
verses.decoded: Get up and stand on your feet, because I have appeared to you to appoint you as a servant and a witness of what you have seen and of what I will show you in the future.

verses.kjv: Delivering thee from the people, and from the Gentiles, unto whom now I send thee,
verses.decoded: I am rescuing you from the people and the Gentiles, and now I am sending you to them.

verses.kjv: To open their eyes, and to turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan unto God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins, and inheritance among them which are sanctified by faith that is in me.
verses.decoded: To open their eyes and turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan to God, so they may receive forgiveness of sins and a place among those who are made holy by faith in me.

verses.kjv: Whereupon, O king Agrippa, I was not disobedient unto the heavenly vision:
verses.decoded: So, King Agrippa, I did not refuse to obey the vision from heaven.

verses.kjv: But shewed first unto them of Damascus, and at Jerusalem, and throughout all the coasts of Judaea, and then to the Gentiles, that they should repent and turn to God, and do works meet for repentance.
verses.decoded: Instead, I first preached to the people in Damascus, then in Jerusalem, and throughout Judea, and finally to the Gentiles, telling them to repent, turn to God, and live lives that show their repentance.

verses.kjv: For these causes the Jews caught me in the temple, and went about to kill me.
verses.decoded: Because of this, the Jews arrested me in the temple and tried to kill me.

verses.kjv: Having therefore obtained help of God, I continue unto this day, witnessing both to small and great, saying none other things than those which the prophets and Moses did say should come:
verses.decoded: But with God's help, I have continued to this day, testifying to both the important and the ordinary people, saying nothing different from what the prophets and Moses said would happen.

verses.kjv: That Christ should suffer, and that he should be the first that should rise from the dead, and should shew light unto the people, and to the Gentiles.
verses.decoded: That the Messiah would suffer, be the first to rise from the dead, and bring light to both the people of Israel and the Gentiles.

verses.kjv: And as he thus spake for himself, Festus said with a loud voice, Paul, thou art beside thyself; much learning doth make thee mad.
verses.decoded: As Paul was speaking, Festus shouted loudly, 'Paul, you are out of your mind! Your great learning is driving you crazy!'

verses.kjv: But he said, I am not mad, most noble Festus; but speak forth the words of truth and soberness.
verses.decoded: Paul replied, 'I am not crazy, honorable Festus. I am speaking the truth and being serious.'

verses.kjv: For the king knoweth of these things, before whom also I speak freely: for I am persuaded that none of these things are hidden from him; for this thing was not done in a corner.
verses.decoded: The king knows about these things, and I speak openly before him because I am sure nothing like this has been kept secret from him; these events did not happen in private.

verses.kjv: King Agrippa, believest thou the prophets? I know that thou believest.
verses.decoded: King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know you do.

verses.kjv: Then Agrippa said unto Paul, Almost thou persuadest me to be a Christian.
verses.decoded: Then Agrippa said to Paul, 'You are almost convincing me to become a Christian.'

verses.kjv: And Paul said, I would to God, that not only thou, but also all that hear me this day, were both almost, and altogether such as I am, except these bonds.
verses.decoded: Paul replied, 'I wish that not only you but everyone listening today were as fully committed to Christ as I am—except for these chains.'

verses.kjv: And when he had thus spoken, the king rose up, and the governor, and Bernice, and they that sat with them:
verses.decoded: After Paul finished speaking, the king, the governor, Bernice, and those sitting with them stood up.

verses.kjv: And when they were gone aside, they talked between themselves, saying, This man doeth nothing worthy of death or of bonds.
verses.decoded: After they left, they talked among themselves, saying, 'This man has done nothing deserving death or imprisonment.'

verses.kjv: Then said Agrippa unto Festus, This man might have been set at liberty, if he had not appealed unto Caesar.
verses.decoded: Then Agrippa said to Festus, 'This man could have been freed if he had not appealed to Caesar.'

verses.kjv: And when it was determined that we should sail into Italy, they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners unto one named Julius, a centurion of Augustus’ band.
verses.decoded: When it was decided that we would sail to Italy, they handed Paul and some other prisoners over to a man named Julius, who was a centurion in the emperor's guard.

verses.kjv: And entering into a ship of Adramyttium, we launched, meaning to sail by the coasts of Asia; one Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, being with us.
verses.decoded: We boarded a ship from Adramyttium and set sail, planning to travel along the coast of Asia. Aristarchus, a Macedonian from Thessalonica, was with us.

verses.kjv: And the next day we touched at Sidon. And Julius courteously entreated Paul, and gave him liberty to go unto his friends to refresh himself.
verses.decoded: The next day we stopped at Sidon. Julius treated Paul kindly and allowed him to visit his friends there to rest and recover.

verses.kjv: And when we had launched from thence, we sailed under Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.
verses.decoded: After leaving Sidon, we sailed along the southern coast of Cyprus because the winds were against us.

verses.kjv: And when we had sailed over the sea of Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra, a city of Lycia.
verses.decoded: After sailing past the seas near Cilicia and Pamphylia, we arrived at Myra, a city in the region of Lycia.

verses.kjv: And there the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing into Italy; and he put us therein.
verses.decoded: There, the centurion found a ship from Alexandria that was heading to Italy, and he put us on board that ship.

verses.kjv: And when we had sailed slowly many days, and scarce were come over against Cnidus, the wind not suffering us, we sailed under Crete, over against Salmone;
verses.decoded: After sailing slowly for many days and barely reaching the area opposite Cnidus because the wind was against us, we sailed along the southern coast of Crete near a place called Salmone.

verses.kjv: And, hardly passing it, came unto a place which is called The fair havens; nigh whereunto was the city of Lasea.
verses.decoded: We barely passed that point and came to a place called Fair Havens, near the city of Lasea.

verses.kjv: Now when much time was spent, and when sailing was now dangerous, because the fast was now already past, Paul admonished them,
verses.decoded: Since a lot of time had passed and sailing was now risky because the religious fast had already ended, Paul warned them.

verses.kjv: And said unto them, Sirs, I perceive that this voyage will be with hurt and much damage, not only of the lading and ship, but also of our lives.
verses.decoded: He said to them, 'Gentlemen, I believe this trip will result in injury and great damage—not only to the cargo and the ship but also to our lives.'

verses.kjv: Nevertheless the centurion believed the master and the owner of the ship, more than those things which were spoken by Paul.
verses.decoded: But the centurion trusted the ship’s captain and owner more than what Paul said.

verses.kjv: And because the haven was not commodious to winter in, the more part advised to depart thence also, if by any means they might attain to Phenice, and there to winter; which is an haven of Crete, and lieth toward the south west and north west.
verses.decoded: Since the harbor was not suitable for staying through the winter, most advised leaving to try to reach Phoenix, a harbor on Crete that faces southwest and northwest, where they could spend the winter.

verses.kjv: And when the south wind blew softly, supposing that they had obtained their purpose, loosing thence, they sailed close by Crete.
verses.decoded: When a gentle south wind began to blow, they thought they had achieved their goal, so they set sail and sailed close along the coast of Crete.

verses.kjv: But not long after there arose against it a tempestuous wind, called Euroclydon.
verses.decoded: But soon a violent storm called Euroclydon came against them.

verses.kjv: And when the ship was caught, and could not bear up into the wind, we let her drive.
verses.decoded: When the ship was caught by the storm and could not face the wind, we let it be driven by the wind.

verses.kjv: And running under a certain island which is called Clauda, we had much work to come by the boat:
verses.decoded: We sailed close to an island called Clauda, and it was difficult to get the small boat alongside.

verses.kjv: Which when they had taken up, they used helps, undergirding the ship; and, fearing lest they should fall into the quicksands, strake sail, and so were driven.
verses.decoded: After bringing the boat on board, they used ropes to support the ship from underneath. They were afraid the ship might run onto quicksand, so they lowered the sails and were driven by the wind.

verses.kjv: And we being exceedingly tossed with a tempest, the next day they lightened the ship;
verses.decoded: We were violently shaken by the storm, and the next day they threw some cargo overboard to lighten the ship.

verses.kjv: And the third day we cast out with our own hands the tackling of the ship.
verses.decoded: On the third day, we threw the ship’s ropes and rigging overboard with our own hands.

verses.kjv: And when neither sun nor stars in many days appeared, and no small tempest lay on us, all hope that we should be saved was then taken away.
verses.decoded: For many days, neither the sun nor stars were visible, and a fierce storm continued. We lost all hope of being saved.

verses.kjv: But after long abstinence Paul stood forth in the midst of them, and said, Sirs, ye should have hearkened unto me, and not have loosed from Crete, and to have gained this harm and loss.
verses.decoded: After going without food for a long time, Paul stood up and said, 'Men, you should have listened to me and not sailed from Crete. Then you wouldn’t have suffered this damage and loss.'

verses.kjv: And now I exhort you to be of good cheer: for there shall be no loss of any man’s life among you, but of the ship.
verses.decoded: Now I encourage you to be brave; none of you will lose your lives, only the ship will be destroyed.

verses.kjv: For there stood by me this night the angel of God, whose I am, and whom I serve,
verses.decoded: Last night, the angel of God, whom I belong to and serve, stood beside me,

verses.kjv: Saying, Fear not, Paul; thou must be brought before Caesar: and, lo, God hath given thee all them that sail with thee.
verses.decoded: and said, 'Don’t be afraid, Paul. You must appear before Caesar, and God has given you all the people sailing with you.'

verses.kjv: Wherefore, sirs, be of good cheer: for I believe God, that it shall be even as it was told me.
verses.decoded: So, men, take courage! I trust God that everything will happen just as He said.

verses.kjv: Howbeit we must be cast upon a certain island.
verses.decoded: However, we will be shipwrecked on a certain island.

verses.kjv: But when the fourteenth night was come, as we were driven up and down in Adria, about midnight the shipmen deemed that they drew near to some country;
verses.decoded: On the fourteenth night, as we were tossed around the Adriatic Sea, the sailors thought they were getting close to land around midnight.

verses.kjv: And sounded, and found it twenty fathoms: and when they had gone a little further, they sounded again, and found it fifteen fathoms.
verses.decoded: They measured the water depth and found it was 20 fathoms (120 feet). After moving a little farther, they measured again and found 15 fathoms (90 feet).

verses.kjv: Then fearing lest we should have fallen upon rocks, they cast four anchors out of the stern, and wished for the day.
verses.decoded: Fearing they might hit rocks, they dropped four anchors from the back of the ship and waited for daylight.

verses.kjv: And as the shipmen were about to flee out of the ship, when they had let down the boat into the sea, under colour as though they would have cast anchors out of the foreship,
verses.decoded: The sailors were preparing to escape by lowering the small boat into the sea, pretending they were just dropping anchors from the front of the ship.

verses.kjv: Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, Except these abide in the ship, ye cannot be saved.
verses.decoded: Paul told the centurion and the soldiers that unless the people stay on the ship, they cannot be saved.

verses.kjv: Then the soldiers cut off the ropes of the boat, and let her fall off.
verses.decoded: Then the soldiers cut the ropes holding the lifeboat and let it drift away.

verses.kjv: And while the day was coming on, Paul besought them all to take meat, saying, This day is the fourteenth day that ye have tarried and continued fasting, having taken nothing.
verses.decoded: As morning approached, Paul urged everyone to eat something, saying it was the fourteenth day they had been waiting and fasting without food.

verses.kjv: Wherefore I pray you to take some meat: for this is for your health: for there shall not an hair fall from the head of any of you.
verses.decoded: So he asked them to eat for their own good, assuring them that not a single hair on their heads would be lost.

verses.kjv: And when he had thus spoken, he took bread, and gave thanks to God in presence of them all: and when he had broken it, he began to eat.
verses.decoded: After saying this, Paul took some bread, thanked God in front of everyone, broke it, and began to eat.

verses.kjv: Then were they all of good cheer, and they also took some meat.
verses.decoded: This encouraged everyone, and they all started eating some food.

verses.kjv: And we were in all in the ship two hundred threescore and sixteen souls.
verses.decoded: There were 276 people on the ship in total.

verses.kjv: And when they had eaten enough, they lightened the ship, and cast out the wheat into the sea.
verses.decoded: After eating enough, they made the ship lighter by throwing the wheat cargo into the sea.

verses.kjv: And when it was day, they knew not the land: but they discovered a certain creek with a shore, into the which they were minded, if it were possible, to thrust in the ship.
verses.decoded: When daylight came, they couldn’t identify the land but saw a bay with a beach and planned to try to steer the ship there if possible.

verses.kjv: And when they had taken up the anchors, they committed themselves unto the sea, and loosed the rudder bands, and hoised up the mainsail to the wind, and made toward shore.
verses.decoded: They lifted the anchors, trusted themselves to the sea, untied the rudder ropes, raised the main sail to catch the wind, and headed toward the shore.

verses.kjv: And falling into a place where two seas met, they ran the ship aground; and the forepart stuck fast, and remained unmoveable, but the hinder part was broken with the violence of the waves.
verses.decoded: The ship ran aground where two bodies of water met; the front part got stuck and didn’t move, but the back part was broken by the strong waves.

verses.kjv: And the soldiers’ counsel was to kill the prisoners, lest any of them should swim out, and escape.
verses.decoded: The soldiers planned to kill the prisoners to prevent any from swimming away and escaping.

verses.kjv: But the centurion, willing to save Paul, kept them from their purpose; and commanded that they which could swim should cast themselves first into the sea, and get to land:
verses.decoded: But the centurion, wanting to save Paul, stopped them and ordered those who could swim to jump into the sea first and get to shore.

verses.kjv: And the rest, some on boards, and some on broken pieces of the ship. And so it came to pass, that they escaped all safe to land.
verses.decoded: The rest got to shore on pieces of wood or broken parts of the ship. In this way, everyone safely reached land.

verses.kjv: And when they were escaped, then they knew that the island was called Melita.
verses.decoded: After they got safely to shore, they realized the island was called Malta.

verses.kjv: And the barbarous people shewed us no little kindness: for they kindled a fire, and received us every one, because of the present rain, and because of the cold.
verses.decoded: The local people, though considered uncivilized, showed us great kindness by lighting a fire and welcoming everyone because it was raining and cold.

verses.kjv: And when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks, and laid them on the fire, there came a viper out of the heat, and fastened on his hand.
verses.decoded: Paul collected some sticks and put them on the fire, and a poisonous snake came out from the heat and bit his hand.

verses.kjv: And when the barbarians saw the venomous beast hang on his hand, they said among themselves, No doubt this man is a murderer, whom, though he hath escaped the sea, yet vengeance suffereth not to live.
verses.decoded: When the locals saw the snake hanging on his hand, they said to each other, 'This man must be a murderer. Even though he survived the shipwreck, justice won’t let him live.'

verses.kjv: And he shook off the beast into the fire, and felt no harm.
verses.decoded: Paul shook the snake off into the fire and was not hurt at all.

verses.kjv: Howbeit they looked when he should have swollen, or fallen down dead suddenly: but after they had looked a great while, and saw no harm come to him, they changed their minds, and said that he was a god.
verses.decoded: They expected him to swell up or suddenly die, but after watching him for a long time and seeing no harm, they changed their minds and said he must be a god.

verses.kjv: In the same quarters were possessions of the chief man of the island, whose name was Publius; who received us, and lodged us three days courteously.
verses.decoded: Nearby was the home of the island’s leading man, Publius, who welcomed us and kindly hosted us for three days.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, that the father of Publius lay sick of a fever and of a bloody flux: to whom Paul entered in, and prayed, and laid his hands on him, and healed him.
verses.decoded: Publius’s father was sick with a fever and severe diarrhea. Paul went to him, prayed, placed his hands on him, and healed him.

verses.kjv: So when this was done, others also, which had diseases in the island, came, and were healed:
verses.decoded: After that, many others on the island who were sick came to Paul and were healed.

verses.kjv: Who also honoured us with many honours; and when we departed, they laded us with such things as were necessary.
verses.decoded: They showed us great respect and when we left, they gave us everything we needed for the journey.

verses.kjv: And after three months we departed in a ship of Alexandria, which had wintered in the isle, whose sign was Castor and Pollux.
verses.decoded: After three months, we left on an Alexandrian ship that had stayed through the winter on the island; its emblem was Castor and Pollux.

verses.kjv: And landing at Syracuse, we tarried there three days.
verses.decoded: We landed at Syracuse and stayed there for three days.

verses.kjv: And from thence we fetched a compass, and came to Rhegium: and after one day the south wind blew, and we came the next day to Puteoli:
verses.decoded: From there we sailed around the coast to Rhegium. The next day, a south wind came, and the day after that we reached Puteoli.

verses.kjv: Where we found brethren, and were desired to tarry with them seven days: and so we went toward Rome.
verses.decoded: At Puteoli, we met fellow believers who invited us to stay for seven days. After that, we continued on toward Rome.

verses.kjv: And from thence, when the brethren heard of us, they came to meet us as far as Appii forum, and The three taverns: whom when Paul saw, he thanked God, and took courage.
verses.decoded: When the believers heard we were coming, they came out to meet us as far as Appii Forum and the Three Taverns. When Paul saw them, he thanked God and felt encouraged.

verses.kjv: And when we came to Rome, the centurion delivered the prisoners to the captain of the guard: but Paul was suffered to dwell by himself with a soldier that kept him.
verses.decoded: When we arrived in Rome, the centurion handed over the prisoners to the captain of the guard, but Paul was allowed to live by himself with a soldier assigned to guard him.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass, that after three days Paul called the chief of the Jews together: and when they were come together, he said unto them, Men and brethren, though I have committed nothing against the people, or customs of our fathers, yet was I delivered prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans.
verses.decoded: After three days, Paul called the Jewish leaders together. When they arrived, he said, 'Brothers, I have done nothing wrong against our people or their customs, yet I was handed over as a prisoner from Jerusalem to the Romans.'

verses.kjv: Who, when they had examined me, would have let me go, because there was no cause of death in me.
verses.decoded: After they examined me, the Romans wanted to release me because they found no reason to put me to death.

verses.kjv: But when the Jews spake against it, I was constrained to appeal unto Caesar; not that I had ought to accuse my nation of.
verses.decoded: But when the Jewish leaders opposed this, I had to appeal to Caesar, even though I have no complaints against my own people.

verses.kjv: For this cause therefore have I called for you, to see you, and to speak with you: because that for the hope of Israel I am bound with this chain.
verses.decoded: That is why I asked to see you and talk with you—because I am here in chains for the hope of Israel.

verses.kjv: And they said unto him, We neither received letters out of Judaea concerning thee, neither any of the brethren that came shewed or spake any harm of thee.
verses.decoded: They replied, 'We have not received any letters from Judea about you, nor have any of the believers who came told us anything bad about you.'

verses.kjv: But we desire to hear of thee what thou thinkest: for as concerning this sect, we know that every where it is spoken against.
verses.decoded: But we want to hear from you what you think, because we know this group is criticized everywhere.

verses.kjv: And when they had appointed him a day, there came many to him into his lodging; to whom he expounded and testified the kingdom of God, persuading them concerning Jesus, both out of the law of Moses, and out of the prophets, from morning till evening.
verses.decoded: They set a day for him, and many came to his home. Paul explained and testified about God's kingdom, trying to convince them about Jesus using the Law of Moses and the prophets, from morning until evening.

verses.kjv: And some believed the things which were spoken, and some believed not.
verses.decoded: Some believed what Paul said, but others did not.

verses.kjv: And when they agreed not among themselves, they departed, after that Paul had spoken one word, Well spake the Holy Ghost by Esaias the prophet unto our fathers,
verses.decoded: When they couldn’t agree with each other, they left after Paul said one thing: 'The Holy Spirit spoke well through the prophet Isaiah to our ancestors.'

verses.kjv: Saying, Go unto this people, and say, Hearing ye shall hear, and shall not understand; and seeing ye shall see, and not perceive:
verses.decoded: 'Go to this people and say: You will hear but not understand; you will see but not perceive.'

verses.kjv: For the heart of this people is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes have they closed; lest they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them.
verses.decoded: 'The hearts of these people have become insensitive; their ears are hard of hearing, and they have closed their eyes so they won’t see, hear, understand, turn to God, and be healed.'

verses.kjv: Be it known therefore unto you, that the salvation of God is sent unto the Gentiles, and that they will hear it.
verses.decoded: So know this: God’s salvation has been sent to the Gentiles, and they will listen.

verses.kjv: And when he had said these words, the Jews departed, and had great reasoning among themselves.
verses.decoded: After Paul said these things, the Jewish leaders left and debated among themselves.

verses.kjv: And Paul dwelt two whole years in his own hired house, and received all that came in unto him,
verses.decoded: Paul stayed two full years in his rented house and welcomed everyone who came to see him.

verses.kjv: Preaching the kingdom of God, and teaching those things which concern the Lord Jesus Christ, with all confidence, no man forbidding him.
verses.decoded: He was boldly preaching about God's kingdom and teaching about the Lord Jesus Christ without anyone stopping him.
